input.question: Could this solar flare potentially destroy the earth?
input.ground_truth: I visited NOAA's space weather prediction center last month and wrote a [brief article](_URL_0_) about this if you're looking to find out more. The upshot - yes a huge storm could seriously harm the electrical grid and communications network if we are not prepared for it. It could not "wipe out" countries or directly physically harm anyone on the Earth's surface though.

Now, if your friend sneezes a little, it might make you jump, but it won’t hurt you. But if your friend sneezes super, super hard—like the biggest sneeze ever—could it hurt you? Well, the sun’s biggest sneezes (the biggest solar flares) are really, really strong, but they can’t actually break the Earth or destroy it.

The Earth has a big invisible shield called the magnetosphere, kind of like a big umbrella, that helps protect us from most of the sun’s sneezes. Sometimes, if the sneeze is very, very big, it might make some things on Earth go funny, like making the lights go out for a little while, but it can’t break or destroy the whole Earth.

So, even if the sun sneezes really hard, the Earth is safe!
